title: Koko Eating Bananas
hints: Trying every speed k = 1, 2, 3, ... and checking each in O(n) works but is O(n * max(piles)). What property of 'speed k is fast enough' lets you skip most speeds?
Feasibility is monotone: if speed k finishes within h hours, every speed above k does too. A monotone yes/no predicate over a range of integers is exactly what binary search needs.
Hours needed at speed k is sum(ceil(p / k)) over the piles, which is (p + k - 1) // k in integers. Binary search k over [1, max(piles)] for the smallest feasible value.
